components.gap: Supply Grinstead and Snell's stated equivalent form of mutual independence (Def. 4.2, p. 141: A1,...,An are mutually independent exactly when, for every choice of each Ai or its complement, the probability of the full intersection is the product of the probabilities; the case n = 3 is Exercise 33, p. 155) and their claim that the single identity P(A1 and ... and An) = P(A1)...P(An) does not imply mutual independence (p. 141, with the six-point example of Exercise 8, p. 151). The definition entry gives only the subset-product form; on the route the general chapter proves only that complementing independent events preserves independence (thm:p15-independence-basic, item 2) and remarks that checking the full intersection alone is not the definition (def:p15-general-independence), so neither the converse equivalence nor the non-implication with a counterexample is supplied.

components.gap: Supply Durrett's notation for special cases of the integral (sec. 1.4, pp. 23-24): the integral of f(x) dx for Lebesgue measure on R^d; the integral from a to b of f(x) dx for the integral over E = [a,b]; the integral of f(x) dG(x) for the Stieltjes measure with mu((a,b]) = G(b) - G(a); and the sum over i in Omega of f(i) for counting measure on a countable set, with his remark that results for sums follow from those for integrals.
